# Best family lawyers on Brisbane’s Northside

If you’re looking for a reputable family lawyer around Chermside or North Lakes, I’d prioritise firms with a dedicated family law practice, experience handling parenting disputes and property settlements, transparent fees, and convenient access for appointments.

The best fit depends on whether you need help with separation, children and parenting arrangements, dividing assets, divorce, or a more complex dispute involving domestic and family violence. A firm's reputation is important, but so is finding a lawyer who communicates clearly and gives realistic advice about costs and likely outcomes.

## How I would choose between them

| If your priority is… | Start by contacting |
|--------|--------|
| Convenient Chermside location | Barton Family Lawyers |
| North Lakes location and a family-law-focused team | ABA Family Lawyers or Best Wilson Buckley |
| Mediation and negotiated agreements | Macpherson Family Law or Koolik & Associates |
| A lawyer with an identified specialist credential | Zande Law |
| Family law plus potentially related legal issues | Preston & Associates |


These are starting points based on practice focus, location and available credentials, not guarantees of results.

## Five questions to ask before hiring

1. **Who will personally handle my case?** Ask about their family law experience and whether they are an Accredited Specialist in Family Law.
2. **What will it cost?** Request the initial consultation fee, hourly rate, likely total cost and any fixed-fee stages in writing.
3. **What is the likely strategy?** Ask whether negotiation, mediation or court proceedings are appropriate for your circumstances.
4. **Who will keep me updated?** Find out how quickly they respond and whether you will deal with the same solicitor throughout.
5. **Have you handled cases like mine?** Ask for relevant experience with parenting disputes, complex assets, businesses, superannuation or domestic violence, as applicable.

For an independent check, you can use the [Queensland Law Society's Find a Solicitor service](https://www.qls.com.au/For-the-community/Find-a-solicitor) to verify practising details and specialist accreditation. Doyle's Guide is another useful reference for peer-recognised Brisbane family law firms. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/family-divorce-law-firms-brisbane/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.qls.com.au](https://www.qls.com.au/register-of-solicitors/preston-and-associates?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**My recommendation\:** Start with two or three initial consultations rather than choosing purely on online star ratings. The right lawyer should explain your options in plain English, be candid about the risks, and give you a clear understanding of fees.

One question that would help me narrow this down further: **what type of family law matter do you need help with — parenting/children, property settlement, divorce, or domestic violence?** The strongest shortlist may differ considerably depending on the issue.

These are starting points based on practice focus, location and available credentials, not guarantees of results.

## Five questions to ask before hiring

1. **Who will personally handle my case?** Ask about their family law experience and whether they are an Accredited Specialist in Family Law.
2. **What will it cost?** Request the initial consultation fee, hourly rate, likely total cost and any fixed-fee stages in writing.
3. **What is the likely strategy?** Ask whether negotiation, mediation or court proceedings are appropriate for your circumstances.
4. **Who will keep me updated?** Find out how quickly they respond and whether you will deal with the same solicitor throughout.
5. **Have you handled cases like mine?** Ask for relevant experience with parenting disputes, complex assets, businesses, superannuation or domestic violence, as applicable.

For an independent check, you can use the [Queensland Law Society's Find a Solicitor service](https://www.qls.com.au/For-the-community/Find-a-solicitor) to verify practising details and specialist accreditation. Doyle's Guide is another useful reference for peer-recognised Brisbane family law firms. [doylesguide.com](https://doylesguide.com/rankings/family-divorce-law-firms-brisbane/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.qls.com.au](https://www.qls.com.au/register-of-solicitors/preston-and-associates?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**My recommendation\:** Start with two or three initial consultations rather than choosing purely on online star ratings. The right lawyer should explain your options in plain English, be candid about the risks, and give you a clear understanding of fees.

One question that would help me narrow this down further: **what type of family law matter do you need help with — parenting/children, property settlement, divorce, or domestic violence?** The strongest shortlist may differ considerably depending on the issue.
